payment.q: Which payment methods do you accept?

access.q: How long do I have access to the course?
access.a: Access is for life: once enrolled, you can watch the lessons as often as you like, with no time limit.

mobile.q: Can I follow the course on my phone?
mobile.a: Yes, the platform works on smartphone, tablet and computer. An internet connection is all you need.

abroad.q: Can I follow the course from outside Spain?
abroad.a: Yes. Everything is online, with lifetime access on phone, tablet or computer: you follow the course wherever you live. The rules, procedures and authorities covered are Spain's, where the development takes place.

invoice.a: Yes, an invoice can be issued on request after payment. Write to us with your order reference.

support.a: Our team answers by email and by phone or WhatsApp during office hours, and helps you with any technical issue.

modules.q: Do I have to buy everything at once?
modules.a: No. Modules are sold one by one, depending on where you are. Discounts grow with the number of modules, and full access remains the cheapest option per module.

partners.a: Yes. Each module ends with the institutions and partners to go to in your province for that phase, from the course's directory of the 52 provinces, with your region's planning law and taxes. Names of professional bodies and agencies are confirmed in their official search engines. Construye takes no commission on these introductions.

projectType.q: Does it suit my type of project?
projectType.a: The course follows an open-market housing development, from the plot to after-sales. Much of the journey — land, permits, financing, construction, legalisation — is the same for commercial and mixed-use schemes. Subsidised housing adds requirements set by each region that are not covered in detail.

phases.a: The laws that apply and where to go, its lessons in writing, an action checklist for your own project, the institutions and partners of your province, and a quiz to check what you learnt. You can follow the modules in order or go straight to the one you need.

hero.title: Property development in Spain, phase by phase: from the plot to the handover of the keys.
hero.body: The 12 phases of an open-market housing development, in the order they really happen: what each one involves, the documents, the authorities, the timescales and the mistakes that cost the most.
hero.paymentNote: Lifetime access: phone, tablet, computer. As a whole or module by module.

maze.title: Capital is not enough. It is the paperwork that stops projects.
maze.lead: You have the funds, perhaps even the plot. What blocks you comes later.
maze.close: These are not money problems: they are about order, documents and timing. They are learnt over years in the trade — or by paying for them.

costOfError.title: In a development, a mistake is not paid in euros. It is paid in months.
costOfError.e1: A plot bought without checking its buildable area: the project that does not fit on it.
costOfError.e2: An incomplete permit application: months of waiting with the land paid and interest running.
costOfError.e3: Taking buyers' money without a guarantee or a special account: a breach of the law, and a bank that will not lend.
costOfError.e4: The wrong builder: works stopped, budget reopened, handover delayed.
costOfError.close: The price of this course? What it would cost you to learn just one of these phases on your own site.

method.title: The whole journey: from the plot to the handover of the keys.
method.intro: The real order of an open-market housing development, without skipping a phase:
method.s1: Plot: search, planning analysis, due diligence and purchase, with your own or external financing.
method.s2: Feasibility study: market research, costs, revenue and profitability.
method.s3: Design: technical studies, preliminary design, basic and construction projects, professional approval (visado) and the Health and Safety Plan.
method.s4: Permits: building permit, authorisations, administrative requirements and grant.
method.s5: Financing and contracting: developer loan, insurance, tender and construction contracts.
method.s6: Construction: foundations, structure, envelope, services and finishes, from the setting-out record to the completion record.
method.s7: Site control: site management team, technical inspection body, quality, budget, planning and ten-year insurance.
method.s8: Sales: marketing, reservations, contracts and buyer follow-up.
method.s9: Legalisation: completion, technical documentation, first-occupation licence and Land Registry.
method.s10: Pre-handover: inspections, snagging, documentation and coordination with the notary.
method.s11: Handover of the keys: deeds, building logbook, utilities, owners' association, final payment and delivery of possession.
method.s12: After-sales and close-out: information to the owners' association, warranties, claims and winding up the development.
method.close: At every phase: what to do, in what order, with which document — and the mistake that costs the most at that exact moment.
